signals.headline: Namespace closes $42M Series B funding round
signals.quote: Namespace recently closed a $42 million Series B round led by Scale Venture Partners, with participation from NEA, 20VC
signals.how_to_use: Reference their October 2026 Series B raise when reaching out to founders about updating D&O coverage limits for the growth stage.
signals.found_by: Looks up the company's Form D filings, which are due within 15 days of a first sale, and searches news for the round announcement.
signals.why_it_matters: Investors commonly require D&O within 60 to 90 days of close, and new board seats mean new personal liability.
signals.angle: Investors commonly require D&O within 60 to 90 days of close. Ask whether D&O is already in place for the new board.

signals.headline: Namespace is expanding enterprise customer adoption and large-scale deployments
signals.quote: Today, we power software development for more than 1,000 of the world's most ambitious companies, including
signals.how_to_use: Connect their upmarket traction with enterprise accounts like ClassPass and Framer to the need for comprehensive Tech E&O and Cyber Liability coverage.
signals.found_by: Reads every open role and flags enterprise-sales, solutions and compliance titles. Fetches the company's security, trust, customers and enterprise pages.
signals.why_it_matters: Enterprise procurement asks for a certificate of insurance before signing. This is usually the first hard insurance deadline a startup hits, and a deal is waiting on it.
signals.angle: Enterprise customers ask for a certificate of insurance (Tech E&O and cyber) before they sign. Ask whether a deal is waiting on one.

signals.headline: COO Eva Parth Dos Santos posts about customer growth and scaling enterprise dependencies
signals.quote: Some years ago, I would never have thought that great companies like Framer would depend on something we have built.
signals.how_to_use: Mention COO Eva Parth Dos Santos's public reflection on trusted enterprise deployments like Framer when opening a conversation about scaling operational insurance.
signals.found_by: Runs one search per top contact for their recent public posts, interviews and announcements, and keeps only results that name both the person and the company.
signals.why_it_matters: It is the most personal opener available: something that person chose to say in public.
signals.angle: Open with what they said and where, then connect it to the insurance requirement it creates.

signals.headline: Open roles in 3 US states
signals.quote: Roles located in 3 US states: NY (7), CA (6), VA (1).
signals.how_to_use: Each new state with an employee needs workers' comp there. Ask whether coverage follows the hiring plan.
signals.found_by: Reads the location of every open role and counts the distinct US states. If the company has no job board, its own careers page is read instead. For a company based abroad, one US role is enough.
signals.why_it_matters: Workers' comp is required state by state, from the first employee in each one. Headcount growth also raises employment-practices risk.
signals.angle: Each new state with an employee needs workers' comp there. Ask whether coverage follows the hiring plan.

rejected.reason: The blog posts and news refer to customer use cases or third-party storage features rather than an internal proprietary AI product launch by Namespace in the last 6 months.
Articles mention data center expansion globally, but no specific new office lease or corporate HQ move was announced within the last 6 months.
